---
title: "The explicit kernelspec form"
jupyter:
  kernelspec:
    name: juphyter-render
    language: php
    display_name: "PHP (juphyter render tests)"
---

The second way of selecting a kernel states the name, the language, and the
display name outright, which is the form Jupyter itself writes into a notebook.
As it stands above it fails, because Quarto's jupyter engine also reads the
directory the kernelspec was found in and only `jupyter: <name>` fills that in.
A test renders this document twice, once as it is and once with `path` added, so
that both the limitation and the fix for it stay true.

```{php}
$widths = ['name' => 7, 'language' => 3];

sprintf('%d fields, %d characters', count($widths), array_sum($widths));
```
